sources.title: On local Type I singularities of the Navier-Stokes equations and Liouville theorems
claims_used: Type-I singular suitable solutions are equivalent, in the paper's formulation, to existence of a nontrivial mild bounded ancient solution with finite I.
A,C,D,E are nonnegative scale-invariant local magnitudes and I is their supremum over parabolic balls.
Suitable weak solutions obey the local-energy inequality with the signed cutoff terms involving (partial_t+Delta)zeta and (|v|^2+2q)v dot grad zeta.
The local pressure can be decomposed into a Calderon-Zygmund part from localized v tensor v plus a harmonic remainder.
The separate global-L3 backward-sequence Liouville theorem requires a stronger trajectory/global hypothesis than local finite-I bookkeeping.

direct_calculation_not_literature_claim: The pressure-free shear and recrossing witness in C001 are verified directly from the Navier-Stokes equation and smooth local-energy identity; no source is cited for that calculation.
negative_history_preserved: No source was interpreted as proving finite-I itself supplies a sign/no-recrossing law.
No current 2026 theorem was found or claimed to close the global finite-I ancient no-return residual in this cycle.
